headline: A 42-light-year X-ray tail links a pulsar to previously 'orphan' gamma rays
summary: Understanding the origin, acceleration and propagation of high-energy cosmic rays has been a century-old mystery in astrophysics. The tail extends about 42 light-years (250 trillion miles) and stretches in the same direction as ultrahigh-energy gamma-ray emission detected by LHAASO, with the two showing a close spatial match.

headline: Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system to fend off particles from the sun

headline: From spider webs to mosaics: How nanosheets of graphene oxide control the patterns left by a drying droplet
